newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - July 10.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - July 10.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:
WASHINGTON - The U.S. Federal Communications Commission blocks a step toward regulating spirits advertisements on radio and television.
LUXEMBOURG - The European Court of Justice tells Sweden it cannot apply its national ban on advertising aimed at children to broadcasters based in Britain.
FRANKFURT - Demand for public relations agencies is growing among companies involved in international business, the German Association of Public Relations Agencies says.

PARIS - France's smallest private general terrestrial television station, M6, is increasing its share of the TV advertising market in line with growth in its audience and improvements in its image, managing director Nicolas deTavernost says.
LONDON - JWT Media, part of the J. Walter Thompson advertising agency owned by WPP Group Plc, says it will undertake a global project on media research, planning systems development and training.
BONN - German Communications Association BDW says luxury auto maker Audi has won its award for excellence in advertising and marketing for 1997.
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

NEW YORK - Microsoft Corp will shift the focus of its Microsoft Network to information and service-oriented programming and away from the television-style programming that it announced last autumn, The Wall Street Journal says in its electronic edition.

SANTA CLARA, Calif. - Yahoo! Inc. reports a better-than-expected second quarter profit of $610,000 or two cents a share, helped by growth in traffic on its Internet navigation site on the World Wide Web. Traffic on the Internet site grew more than 26 percent to an average 38 million page views a day during the month of June, compared with more than 30 million in March.

SYDNEY - The government-owned Australian Broadcasting Corp announces it has sold its Asian satellite television channel, Australia Television, to budding television mogul Kerry Stokes and his Seven Network. The English-language satellite service broadcasts to a potential audience of 20 million.

NEW YORK - Dow Jones & Co says second quarter profit fell nearly 33 percent over a year ago, with its troubled financial information unit hardly breaking even. Total quarterly earnings dropped to $34.9 million, or $0.36 per share, versus $52 million, or $0.54.
PARIS - French television channels have been showing less violence in programmes likely to be seen by children, thanks to a voluntary code put in place last year, France's broadcasting watchdog says.

WASHINGTON - Major U.S. television networks and cable broadcasters agree to modify the current age-based ratings system to better identify program content, avoiding a threat by Congress to pass a law mandating changes.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

BEIJING - French automaker PSA Peugeot Citroen will push its Peugeot brand in China even after its expected withdrawal from a foundering joint venture in the southern city of Guangzhou, a company official says.
CHICAGO - McDonald's Corp. says it will decentralise its U.S. operations into five geographic areas to move decision-making and accountability closer to the restaurant level.
BEIJING - Several foreign colour television makers have slashed prices in China this year, triggering fierce competition with domestic makers, the Securities Daily says.

TURIN - Italy's car-buying incentive program is continuing to boost the domestic auto market, but for the first time in several months dealers are beginning to see signs of slackening demand, car sector research body CSP says.
TOKYO - Nintendo Co Ltd's shares jump fuelled by robust sales of its new Star Fox 64 video game software in the U.S., brokers say.
PARIS - Remy-Cointreau says it may be interested in drink brands up for sale as the result of a planned merger of the drinks businesses of Guinness Plc and Grand Metropolitan Plc.
CONSUMER TRENDS:

NEW YORK - U.S.- based multinational firms are replacing significant numbers of their American managers overseas with local staff, to slash the costs of maintaining executives abroad and because local workers frequently respond better to a manager of their own nationality, industry experts say.

NEW DELHI - Ad agency Ogilvy & Mather has pinned a name on today's generation of young Asians "Genie". "Genie stands for Generation who independently engage in society," Mark Blair, O&M's regional planning director for Asia-Pacific, says.

MOSCOW - Pineapples are cheaper than potatoes in the southern Russian port of Taganrog at the moment because dockers are being paid with tins of the exotic fruit rather than in roubles, Itar-Tass news agency says.
